newsitem.title: GERMANY: Telecoms-driven German bourse starts steady.
newsitem.headline: Telecoms-driven German bourse starts steady.

text.p: Telecommunications were the buzzword as the German share market opened stable dealings on Wednesday morning, after utility group RWE AG revealed a surprise shift in allegiances in this key sector.
The news boosted RWE and its prospective German partner Veba AG in early bourse trade while Viag AG, which had been expected to link up with RWE, dropped.
"Telecoms are certainly the big news today," said a Frankfurt dealer.
The overall market was steady, with the 30-share DAX index up 7.87 points at 2,699.04 at 0850 GMT.
Dealers said they expected the DAX to remain stable around the 2,700 level, continuing its consolidation after a succession of record highs.

Strong activity was again expected on the MDAX index of around 70 medium-sized stocks. Driven by interest in sports goods manufacturer Adidas AG, the MDAX reached new highs on Tuesday while the blue chip DAX declined.
On the DAX itself, Veba and RWE led volumes in early dealings and were up 65 pfennigs at 81.50 marks and 2.20 marks at 59.70 marks respectively.
The activity came after RWE said it had abandoned plans to form a telecoms alliance with Viag and British Telecom and was in the final stages of talks with Veba and Cable & Wireless of the U.K.
"The reactions are pretty predictable -- people are getting out of Viag, getting into Veba and RWE. Telecoms are always a big story here," said a Frankfurt dealer.
RWE said it had pulled out of talks with Viag and BT because of differences in market positioning for Germany's planned E2 mobile telephone network.
